chapter: Nonet, later partnerships and recent projects
title: Ohad Talmor and the eightieth birthday concert
summary: Talmor orchestrated his lines, and Kirchner recalls the Zankel Hall concert.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: In recent years you’ve been doing a lot of stuff with Ohad Talmor. He’s been writing a lot of music for you.

He invited me to send my lines that I was currently writing everyday, just as little exercises, and he orchestrated them, some of them. I appreciated that in a big band context, string quartet context, and a nonet context.
But a different kind of nonet, different instrumentation.
Yeah.
With two bass clarinets as I recall.
Just briefly yeah.
Actually I was at your eightieth birthday concert at Zankel Hall.
That was a nice concert.
It was. In two-thousand and seven
What?
In two-thousand and seven
Will Friedland
“Friedwald”.
. . . Friedwald said “Well, it might’ve been too much of a good thing but it was good to get out in the street at twelve o’clock and get a taxi” or something like that.

He brought that big band from, where was it, Portugal? But also you had Joe Lovano, Steve Swallow, Paul Motian, Ted Brown, Ben Monder; A bunch of good players that you’ve played with in different settings. That was a nice evening.
Yeah. Great. I think George Wein was upstairs listening to Eartha Kitt.
Well you’re still here a she’s not.
Well, that’s a fact.
Exactly.
Don’t know what it means other than that.
